title: 武陵春（风住尘香花已尽）
author: 李清照
intro: A widow in exile at the end of spring: she cannot even bring herself to comb her hair. Friends say the river is lovely and she thinks of a boat trip — but fears the little boat could never carry so much sorrow.
analysis: 这首词是李清照晚年的作品。丈夫已经去世，国家被金兵占了一半，她一个人逃难到浙江金华。上阕写暮春的早上：风停了，花全落了，泥土里还留着花香；太阳很高了，她却懒得梳头。“物是人非事事休”——东西还是原来的东西，人却不在了，一切都完了；想说话，眼泪先流下来。下阕本来有一点希望：听说双溪的春天还很好，也想去划船散心。可马上又担心：那么小的舴艋舟，载不动我这么多的愁。愁本来看不见、摸不着，作者却说它重得船都载不动，这种把抽象的感情写成有重量的东西的手法，非常新鲜，成了千古名句。
analysisEn: Li Qingzhao wrote this late in life. Her husband was dead, northern China had fallen to the Jurchen Jin, and she had fled alone to Jinhua in Zhejiang. The first half is a late-spring morning: the wind has dropped, every blossom has fallen, and only a trace of their scent is left in the dust. The sun is high, yet she has no heart to comb her hair. Then the famous line 物是人非事事休: things are as they were, the person is gone, and nothing matters any more. She wants to speak, but the tears come first. The second half lifts for a moment. People say spring is still lovely at Twin Brooks, the local river, and she thinks she might take a boat out. But at once she doubts it: that little grasshopper boat could never carry so much grief. Sorrow has no weight, of course — giving it one, so heavy it could sink a boat, is what makes the ending unforgettable. Notice how quietly the poem moves: small daily details (hair, flowers, a boat trip) carry a loss too large to name directly.
background: Li Qingzhao (1084–c. 1155) is China’s most celebrated woman poet. After the Jin invasion of 1127 and her husband Zhao Mingcheng’s death in 1129 she lived as a refugee; this lyric is usually dated to 1135, when she was sheltering in Jinhua.
pronunciation: 舴艋 zé měng（小船）；载不动 zài；拟 nǐ；只恐 zhǐ。
version: 采用通行教材文本，题一作《武陵春·春晚》。全词上下两阕，共八句。

lines.zh: 风住尘香花已尽，日晚倦梳头。
lines.rhythm: 风住/尘香/花已尽，日晚/倦梳头
lines.py: fēng zhù chén xiāng huā yǐ jìn, rì wǎn juàn shū tóu
lines.lit: The wind stops, the dust is fragrant, the flowers are all gone; the day is late, too weary to comb my hair.
lines.en: The wind has died; the dust still smells of fallen petals. Though the sun is high, I am too tired to comb my hair.

lines.zh: 物是人非事事休，欲语泪先流。
lines.rhythm: 物是/人非/事事休，欲语/泪先流
lines.py: wù shì rén fēi shì shì xiū, yù yǔ lèi xiān liú
lines.lit: Things are the same, the person is not, everything is over; about to speak, tears flow first.
lines.en: Everything is where it was — but he is gone, and all is finished. I try to speak; the tears come first.

lines.zh: 闻说双溪春尚好，也拟泛轻舟。
lines.rhythm: 闻说/双溪/春尚好，也拟/泛轻舟
lines.py: wén shuō shuāng xī chūn shàng hǎo, yě nǐ fàn qīng zhōu
lines.lit: I hear that at Twin Brooks spring is still fine; I too plan to float a light boat.
lines.en: They say spring is still lovely on Twin Brooks; I think I might take a little boat out.

lines.zh: 只恐双溪舴艋舟，载不动许多愁。
lines.rhythm: 只恐/双溪/舴艋舟，载不动/许多愁
lines.py: zhǐ kǒng shuāng xī zé měng zhōu, zài bù dòng xǔ duō chóu
lines.lit: I only fear the grasshopper boats of Twin Brooks cannot carry so much sorrow.
lines.en: But I fear those tiny boats on Twin Brooks could never hold up this much grief.

words.note: 花落进泥土，泥土都带着花香——暗示花已经落光。

words.en: the sun is late — i.e. the day is far along
words.note: 这里指太阳已经很高，不是傍晚。

words.en: things remain, but the people are gone
words.note: 今天仍是常用成语，形容故地重游、人事全变。
古义“完了、罢了”；现代汉语“休息”“退休”的“休”是停下来。
现代汉语说“还”，书面语“尚未”“尚可”还在用。
现代汉语“拟定”“拟订计划”。
古义，现代汉语多说“划船”；“泛舟”今天仍是书面说法。

words.en: a tiny boat (shaped like a grasshopper)

imagery.name: 落花
imagery.zh: 花已落尽，春天结束了，也像她生命里美好的东西都已经失去。
imagery.en: Every blossom has fallen: spring is over, like all the good things already gone from her life.

imagery.name: 泪
imagery.zh: 话还没出口，泪先流下来，说明悲伤已经压不住了。
imagery.en: The tears come before the words — grief she can no longer hold back.

imagery.name: 船
imagery.zh: 小小的舴艋舟本是散心的工具，却载不动她的愁，把看不见的愁写得有了重量。
imagery.en: A little boat meant for an outing becomes too small to carry her sorrow — grief given real weight.
